cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women aged 18-34 years with singleton pregnancies in Mosul, Iraq, divided into two groups: 50 grand multiparous women and 50 low parity women.
finding: The study found that grand multiparity was associated with a significantly higher incidence of gestational diabetes, anemia, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, cesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage, neonatal intensive care unit admissions, and lower Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was significantly higher in the grand multiparity group compared to the low parity group.
